prerequisites: Knowledge of symbols and codes of electronic components, graphical representations and electrical diagrams
Modeling and simulation in MATLAB/Simulink or equivalent
Ability to install, configure and test sensors, actuators for practical applications
Ability to work in a team and integrate interdisciplinary knowledge

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to conduct experiments, acquire, process, and interpret experimental data.
Ability to theoretically approach, model, and simulate processes and phenomena specific to mechatronic systems.
Ability to analyze and optimize specific problems of mechatronic systems in an interdisciplinary context (mechanical, electronic, informatics) through a systemic approach.
Ability to develop entrepreneurial activities in the field of mechatronics.
Ability for bibliographic documentation and analysis.
Ability to identify the sustainability of innovation directions and/or improvement of processes specific to the field.
Succeeds in identifying and arguing opportunities for applying new concepts, products, or technologies in the field of Mechatronics and Robotics.
Identification of preliminary objectives and priorities in research and design activities, as well as the estimation of potential results.

syllabus_topics: AMR (Automatic Meter Reading) systems for automatic data collection and processing for domestic energy consumption
Telemetering, tele-adjustment, and remote control systems
Functions and component elements of AMR systems
AMR systems for domestic consumption
Monitoring and management of utility supply services
Monitoring and management of natural gas supply
Monitoring and management of water supply
Monitoring of indoor air quality (VOC, CO2, PM2.5 sensors, temperature, humidity)
Mechatronic applications for domestic thermal energy and hot water production
Selection of the heating plant - technical criteria
Gas central heating systems (natural gas and LPG): mechatronic structure, sensors, protections
Solid fuel central heating systems: automation and safety
Operating programs, protections, decision algorithms
Remote control systems (smart thermostats, IoT)
Electric washing machines / dishwashers and dryers as mechatronic systems
Working cycles: washing, dosing, spinning, drying stages
Operational security requirements
Electronic structure: sensors, transducers, actuators (flow meter, pressure switch, BLDC motor, tachometer, solenoid valves, etc.)
The microwave oven as a mechatronic system
Operating principle (electromagnetic field, magnetron)
Security aspects in operation
Block diagram of the control system, power block, sensors, and interlocks
Smart cleaning machines (robot vacuum cleaners, domestic robots)
Working cycles: vacuuming, detection, navigation, mapping (SLAM)
Sensors used: LiDAR, infrared, ultrasonic, dust sensors, gyroscope
Decision and path optimization algorithms
Air conditioning units, indoor air quality control
Operating principles (refrigeration cycle and control)
Transducers and actuators in HVAC
Integrated AMR systems for consumption and comfort optimization
Smart surveillance and security systems for homes
Identification of functions and architecture of security systems
PIR sensors, magnetic sensors, IP cameras, multi-zone systems
Communication, notification, and cloud storage interfaces
RFID technology in domestic and utility applications
Structure of RFID systems
RFID applications in access control, consumption monitoring, domestic logistics
Analysis of mechatronic components in household appliances
Identification of components in a washing machine and a microwave oven
Analysis of the electronic control unit: sensors, actuators, controller
Creation of the functional block diagram
Observation of working cycles and safety functions
Using the oscilloscope and the COMMETER D4141 Datalogger for signal monitoring
Measurement of control signals from sensors (temperature, pressure, humidity)
Use of GW INST EK GDS-1072A-U oscilloscope for visualizing PWM and analog signals
Data acquisition and processing with COMMETER D4141 Datalogger (recording, graphic analysis)
Monitoring energy consumption through AMR (Automatic Meter Reading) systems
Analysis of AMR system structure and operation
Simulation of automatic electricity data collection
Configuration of database connection and real-time consumption visualization
Introduction to RFID technology for user identification
Measurement of PWM signals from ESC and sensors
Analysis of motor response to command variation
Control of thermal systems: heating plants and heat pumps
Study of operating principles for GN/LPG heating plants and heat pumps
Analysis of temperature, pressure, flow sensors
Configuration of automatic thermal control (PID)
Verification of protection and alarm functions
Smart cleaning machines - analysis and diagnostics
Analysis of a robot vacuum cleaner: sensors (LiDAR, IR, ultrasonic), controller, actuators
Study of the navigation algorithm (SLAM)
Testing of autonomous movements and obstacle response
Smart surveillance and security systems
Configuration of an IP video surveillance system with PIR sensors and cameras
Implementation of alerting and remote transmission function via local network or cloud
Analysis and storage of video and sensor data in a database
Final project: design of a mechatronic system for smart services
Design and implementation of an integrated system (e.g., Smart-Room, Smart-Kitchen, Smart-Office)
Selection of appropriate sensors and actuators
Modeling of data flow, control, and feedback
Presentation and demonstration of system operation
Practical testing in a controlled environment
Final report + presentation
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with PowerPoint presentations, video demos, and discussions
Recapitulation of previous concepts and analysis of case studies
Exploration through simulations, practical demonstrations, and laboratory applications (modeling, experiment)
Hands-on activities: assembly, calibration, testing, data analysis, use of oscilloscope and measuring instruments, solving control and adjustment problems of operating parameters
Applied exercises, practical activities, and individual or team projects
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is determined by considering the scores and weights assigned to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded. A grade of 5 certifies the achievement of the minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
